answers.explanation: All ones: every device on the LAN.
The first three bytes. A lookup shows Arcadyan, a Taiwanese maker of ISP gateways.
01:00:5e is the IPv4 multicast range. This one is for 224.0.0.251, multicast DNS.
Second hex digit a: locally administered bit on, multicast bit off. That's why a vendor lookup finds nothing.
dc = 1101 1100: both low bits are 0. Its OUI, dc:46:28, belongs to Intel.
Second hex digit 6 (0110): the locally administered bit is set. It's a phone's private WiFi address.
Those are the digits with bit 1 set and bit 0 clear: 0010, 0110, 1010, 1110.
Cisco's IOS writes MAC addresses that way.
ff is odd, so the group bit is set. Broadcast is the group that contains everyone.
